findings.title: notion-update-page omits allow_async=false and ignores async_task responses, causing race failures and permanent journal lock
findings.impact: Against runtime `notion-update-page` schema `{page_id, command, new_str, allow_async}`, `sync.py` never sends `allow_async: false` (and fails schema validation if required). When Notion returns `{"async_task": ...}`, `update_page` discards the return payload without polling or failing safely; immediate `fetch_page` reads stale content, triggers `push_verify_mismatch`, and permanently locks all future mutating `sync` runs.
findings.recommendation: Set `allow_async: false` whenever present in the discovered `notion-update-page` schema; inspect the parsed response in `update_page` for `async_task` (poll with bounded backoff or fail cleanly with a recoverable async-pending state rather than falsely treating it as completed).

findings.title: Parser only ingests # 附录B; drops all 108 Appendix A group-analysis rows and lacks separate supplement C01-C11 ingestion
findings.attribution_note: Developer task.json only specified `# 附录B` (11 cases / 335 units), so this is primarily a specification gap between the developer task contract and the user's complete goal.
findings.impact: Using `consolidate.py` as-is omits two major substantive Black9 analysis sources required by the user's original goal: (1) all 108 detailed group-analysis table rows in `# 附录A` of the main source file, and (2) the 11x4=44 per-case supplementary segment-research Q&As (`## 二、黑桃11版本逐段补研究` -> `### C01`–`C11`, stopping cleanly before `## 三、思远11版本逐段补研究`) in the separate supplement file.
findings.recommendation: Extend `consolidate.py` to parse `# 附录A` (validating 108 rows and attaching each case's group analyses into its flat case page) and add an optional `--supplement` input extracting `## 二、黑桃11版本逐段补研究` (`### C01`–`C11`, 4 questions each) strictly stopping at `## 三、思远11版本逐段补研究`.

findings.title: Symlinked ancestor directories bypass path safety for state, journal, conflict snapshots, source reads, and bundle output
findings.impact: `check_state_paths_safety` only inspects `state_path.is_symlink()` and immediate `state_path.parent.is_symlink()`; `check_no_symlink_chain(..., stop_at=None)` skips all parent checks despite its docstring; `ensure_safe_file_read` skips even immediate parent checks. Passing `--state <symlink>/nested/state.json` causes `atomic_write_bytes` (`mkdir(parents=True)`) to create directories and write state, journal, and conflict files outside the target tree; `--source <symlink>/s.md` and `--output <symlink>/nested` similarly escape.
findings.recommendation: Walk all non-system ancestor path components (or reject whenever any component along the supplied path is a symlink, accounting cleanly for OS root symlinks like `/var` only if explicitly handled) before any read, `mkdir`, or atomic write.

findings.title: Child pages omit task_marker, allowing --recover to hijack an unrelated page from another parent collection; post-create fetch crash ignores saved page_id
findings.impact: 1) `run_init` journals `page_marker` but never writes it into child page content. When `C01` fails before remote creation under a new parent, `_recover_uncertain_create` misses `pid in parent_body`, falls through to L835-841 matching `title` + `source_sha256`, and silently binds an unrelated `C01` page from an earlier collection under another parent—causing later pushes to overwrite the wrong page. 2) If `create_page` succeeds (saving `page_id` to `state.json`) and immediate `fetch_page` fails, `--recover` ignores the persisted `page_id` and fails when `notion-search` is unavailable or unindexed. 3) If an RPC fails before remote creation and no match exists, `--recover` permanently deadlocks with no operator confirmation path.
findings.recommendation: Verify parent ownership strictly (only accept child pages linked under `collection_parent_id` or bearing an embedded unique `page_marker`), check `state['pages'][doc_id]['page_id']` first during recovery before calling `notion-search`, and provide an explicit audited operator override to resolve verified-absent creations.

findings.title: No recovery path for push journal locks; strict post-push hash equality breaks on Notion URL autolinking; SchemaValidationError poisons journal before send
findings.impact: 1) Any `push_started`, `push_uncertain`, or `push_verify_mismatch` journal state permanently blocks all future mutating `sync` runs, and `init --recover` rejects non-`create_page` operations; operators must hand-edit `.journal.jsonl`. 2) Every generated page includes bare `--source-url` (`https://...`); while `init` tolerates local-vs-remote canonical drift by storing separate baselines, `push` requires exact `verified_canon_sha == local_canon_sha` (L1464), causing Notion autolinking (`[url](url)`) or markdown escaping to fail every push and brick sync. 3) `append_journal(..., 'send_started'/'push_started')` runs before `_build_*_payload` validates schemas, poisoning the journal even when zero requests were sent.
findings.recommendation: Validate payload schemas BEFORE appending `send_started`/`push_started`; normalize Notion autolinks/markdown escapes conservatively or compare against normalized plaintext tokens for post-push verification; add a dedicated `sync --recover` command that fetches remote state and safely reconciles unresolved push ops.

findings.title: extract_notion_content_xml wipes body on literal <content/> and fetch_page accepts unwrapped non-XML responses on pull
findings.impact: 1) `if '<content/>' in normalized` runs before matching `<content>...</content>`; any page body containing literal `<content/>` is erased to `''`, wiping the local file to `'\n'` during `pull`. 2) `fetch_page` discards `had_xml_wrapper`; if `notion-fetch` returns a non-XML truncation/warning message without `isError=true`, `pull` overwrites the local Markdown file with the warning text.
findings.recommendation: Only treat `<content/>` as empty when `<content>...</content>` does not wrap it (anchored inside `<page>`); require `had_xml_wrapper=True` in `sync.py` `fetch_page` (or refuse `pull` on unwrapped/unexpectedly empty responses).

findings.title: Visually ambiguous and non-spoken rows are misclassified and affirmatively labeled as '口播正文记录' (spoken transcript)
findings.impact: `classify_original_cell` defaults any text not matching a narrow hardcoded regex (requiring e.g. `画面:` with colon or specific bracket words) to `spoken_transcript` rendered as `口播正文记录`. Rows such as `画面展示产品对比`, `[特写镜头，推近]`, `（纯动作演示，未说话）`, and `【片头LOGO】` are falsely presented as spoken transcript.
findings.recommendation: Do not label unverified/default rows as spoken transcript; use a neutral default label (`原文单元记录（未独立复听核对）`) and flag bracketed/visual/action-cue rows conservatively as `疑似画面/动作/无对白或混合记录（待复听核验）`.

findings.title: sync.py push omits validate_flat_markdown, allowing tables/codeblocks/nesting that break GitHub Actions safe_two_way
findings.impact: Local edits adding tables, fenced code blocks, blockquotes, or nested lists are pushed to Notion without error because `push` checks only line length `< 1900`, breaking compatibility with the existing GitHub Actions `safe_two_way` engine.
findings.recommendation: Run `consolidate.validate_flat_markdown(local_raw, fname)` before pushing (or gate non-flat pushes behind an explicit opt-in flag).

findings.title: Appendix B parser heading regexes are overly rigid and table column validation is inconsistent
findings.impact: `_CASE_HEADING_RE` rejects `## C10（标题）` and `### C01｜标题`; `_APPENDIX_B_RE` rejects `## 附录B` or `# 附录 B`; `parse_case_table` accepts `len(header_cells) >= 4` at L288 then crashes on `len(cells) != 4` at L304, and silently concatenates multiple 4-column tables if present in one case section.
findings.recommendation: Allow common heading separators (`（`, `(`, space) and configurable/H1-H3 heading levels for Appendix B / C01–C11; enforce exact column header matching consistently.

findings.title: sync.py exits 0 on conflict status; CLI error snippets do not strip echoed private body text
findings.impact: Callers relying on process exit code cannot distinguish `status='conflict'` from `status='ok'` without parsing stdout JSON. Additionally, if `minis-mcp-cli` fails non-zero and echoes CLI payload args on stderr, up to 300 chars could leak non-secret private text.
findings.recommendation: Return a distinct non-zero exit code (e.g., 3) on `status='conflict'`, and avoid echoing raw `proc.stdout`/`proc.stderr` payload snippets without sanitization.
